html:
The movement of thousands of Boer farmers, known as Voortrekkers, out of the British Cape Colony into the interior of southern Africa from 1836 into the 1840s. They went with wagons, cattle and their servants.

They left because they resented British rule: the end of slavery under the Slavery Abolition Act, too little protection on the frontier, and English laws and language.

  • Parties crossed the Orange River and fought the Ndebele of Mzilikazi, who moved north.
  • In Natal, Dingane of the Zulu killed the leader Piet Retief and his men in 1838.
  • At the Battle of Blood River that December, Andries Pretorius's trekkers defeated a large Zulu army.

Britain annexed their republic in Natal in 1843, so many moved on. They founded the Transvaal and the Orange Free State, which lasted until the Boer War. In the 1900s Afrikaner nationalists made the trek into a founding story.
